subject: Finnect: Integration guardrails, SDK liveness, and endpoint migration
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finnect.com>, Jenna Park <jenna.park@finnect.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finnect integration guardrails, SDK liveness, and endpoint migration

Hi Samir / Jenna —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Quick follow-up with the minimal guardrails we recommend for a smooth SDK-driven integration and the migration window planning. High level: make the integration resilient by default and plan a short, staged endpoint cutover (sandbox -> canary -> prod).

Key items (we'll ship a short MAP spreadsheet as an attachment with checkpoints):
- SDK setup: use the 0.13.x runtime client (see snippet in attached sdk-snippets.tar.gz). Initialize with the retry/backoff helper we provide.
- Liveness / warmup: warm up model endpoints for traffic spikes. Recommend a 5-10 minute warmup job before canary traffic.
- Retries/timeouts: client retry policy: 3 attempts, exponential backoff base=250ms, max backoff=2000ms. Per-request timeout: 10s for single-turn text gen; 60s for long streaming sessions.
- Rate limits & quota gating: start with a 60% quota threshold alert and a token-based queue on your side to smooth bursts. We'll enable server-side prefix cache to reduce token spend on repeated prompts.
- Endpoint migration: sandbox -> internal canary (1% traffic) -> expanded canary (10%) -> prod cutover (full). Each stage: health checks, latency check, sample prompt regression.

I've attached a quick MAP (Milestone/Acceptance/Plan) workbook to capture who does what. Monica will coordinate the technical runbook and snippets. Vivek will provide examples for graceful fallback to an earlier model variant in case of regression during canary.

Questions for you before we lock dates:
1) Preferred target cutover week?
2) Any hard requirements on per-hour token budgets?
3) Who on your infra team should we loop in for sandbox traffic routing?

Thanks — happy to sync on a 30m runthrough this week.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

1) Cutover week: target week of June 7 (we need internal approvals first).
2) Token budgets: initially 1.2M tokens / day, but that can ramp. We need backstop controls to avoid accidental overage.
3) Infra contact: Jenna will own sandbox routing and can join the runthrough.

A couple of technical clarifications:

Thanks — we can take the MAP and fill the owner column today.

Samir —

I'll take the MAP and drop in a sprint-level runbook with explicit gating checks. Attached: Finnect-MAP.xlsx (tabbed: Owners, CutoverChecklist). Short notes below that I'll put into the workbook: 

Runbook highlights:
- Pre-canary: sandbox validation, unit tests for token accounting, e2e smoke with synthetic prompts, traffic shaping rules (token limiter on our client -> 200 QPS equivalent).
- Canary: 1% traffic for 2 hours, monitor 95p latency and model regression score (we'll circulate a small testset). Rollback if: latency > 2x baseline OR regression score drops > 3% on eval set.
- Expanded canary: 10% traffic for 24 hours, operational handover to your oncall with a short playbook for fail-open vs fail-closed decisions.

Sample SDK guidance (included in sdk-snippets.tar.gz) — brief inline examples here: 
- init (python): client = RedwoodClient(api_key=ENV['RW_KEY'], timeout=10, retry_policy={"tries":3, "backoff":0.25, "max_backoff":2.0})
- idempotency: attach request_id to top-level metadata; if response is partial, client can reissue with same id and server will attempt dedupe.
- graceful fallback: if model_variant 'm-1.2-q' fails health checks, client should switch to 'm-1.1' for 30 minutes while ops investigates.

I'll schedule a 30m technical sync tomorrow at 10:00 PT if that works for Jenna. 

— Monica

Subject: Re: Finnect integration guardrails, SDK liveness, and endpoint migration

Samir / Jenna —

Quick engineering notes ahead of tomorrow's sync (I'm attaching sdk-snippets.tar.gz with expanded samples):

- Idempotency: we recommend you set a request_id (UUID v4) in metadata. Server-side will attempt best-effort dedupe for 60s. For longer windows use a client-side store of request_id -> response.

- Retries/timeouts (TL;DR): 3 retries, base backoff 250ms, jittered, cap 2000ms, per-request deadline = 10s gen / 60s streaming. If you see repeated 504/timeout clusters during canary, throttle upstream clients or apply a 429-based backoff (recommended sequence: 429 ->  retries with backoff, 502/503 -> circuit-breaker).

- Rate limit shaping: we expose a per-account token budget. We'll provision a soft throttle at 70% of committed tokens with an alert to your SREs. On your side, implement a leaky-bucket queue keyed by user_id (or session_id) to avoid hot-keys. Example pseudo: 
queue.push(request)
if queue.rate(user_id) > user_max: return 429_simulated
process_next()

- Endpoint migration checklist (short): 
1) Confirm sandbox routing and synthetic smoke tests pass.
2) Enable prefix/KV cache for session reuse.
3) Canary: route 1% traffic and run latency+eval checks for 2h. Prepare rollback script: redirect canary traffic back to legacy endpoint and invalidate cache.

- Debugging: enable trace_id on requests (we suggest trace-id = YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<uuid>) so logs correlate across services.

I'll be on the sync to walk through the fallback snippet and the rollback script. If you want, I can also drop a small load generator for the canary window (10m job that exercises common prompt shapes).

— Vivek
